sents.d: Vanity metrics can look good while revenue stays flat.
Follower counts and likes are easy to track but don't necessarily correlate with revenue — it's possible to grow an audience significantly while sales stay completely flat.

Metrics closer to actual business outcomes — leads generated, cost per lead, conversion rate from lead to customer, and average order value — give a much clearer picture of whether marketing efforts are working.

Setting up even basic tracking (which channel a customer came from, tagged links, a simple 'how did you hear about us' question at checkout or booking) makes it possible to double down on what's actually working instead of what simply looks impressive.

take: Measure leads, cost per lead and conversions, not likes.
